authors: A. Michels, J. Gerver, A. Bijl
title: The influence of pressure on the solubility of gases
experimental_method: Synthetic pressure-decline method: a 300 cc stainless-steel tube with the solution and a 10 cc gas volume separated by a valve, rocked for hours in a thermostat (+-0.001 deg); dissolved CH4 from the pressure drop using CH4 isotherm data of Michels and Nederbragt; spring manometers calibrated against a pressure balance.
uncertainties_stated: Manometer accuracy 0.02, 0.1 and 1 atm (ranges 50, 250, 1000 atm); solubility accuracy 'never reach 1%' (i.e. better than 1%) and occasionally of the order of 5% (text p. 801, wording ambiguous); at 100 C 1%, 125 C 1.5% (garbled in scan), 150 C 2% after the vapour correction (p. 804).
quality_remarks: Authors say not much weight was given to highest accuracy (general survey). For 100-150 C a correction for water in the gas phase was estimated by analogy with N2 data (Bartlett). The solubility unit is mol CH4 per mol H2O, not mole fraction. Pressure unit not printed in the table (atm from text and figures). One printed value lacks its decimal point: NaCl 5.4 n 100 C 141.5 atm '0 425' (written 0.425). The same 'n' notation for the non-electrolytes in Table II (e.g. 'Glucose 1n') corresponds to '1 gr. m. per L' in Table I.
